study type: Secondary analysis of registry data (retrospective cohort)
exposure: Induction of labor at 39, 40, or 41 weeks of gestation
Expectant management beyond 39, 40, or 41 weeks of gestation
cohort: The study included 12,676 women with singleton gestations at >=39 weeks of gestational age and a history of one low transverse cesarean delivery, drawn from the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network Cesarean Registry.
finding: Induction of labor at 39 weeks, compared to expectant management, was associated with a significantly higher chance of VBAC but also a higher risk of uterine rupture.
mod_finding: Induction of labor at 39 weeks increased the chance of vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) compared to expectant management.
